title: Field-to-Feature Funnel SprintKit: Account-prioritized Intake and Rapid Scoping
creator: Sofia Martinez
description: Problem: Sales and CS surface high-touch enterprise feature asks in disparate ways (emails, Slack threads, demo notes) which causes duplicated intake tickets, inconsistent priority signals, and friction in scoping. Goal: Create a lightweight, repeatable SprintKit that CS can run to consolidate incoming asks for an account or cluster of accounts, produce a 1-page scoping brief, and map asks to actionable engineering initiatives or backlogs. Scope: non-bug feature requests only; includes templated questions, an account-aware scoring rubric, automated artifact links, and a quick econ proxy. Success metrics: reduce duplicate PM tickets by 40% for high-touch accounts, median time from first ask to PM brief <= 72h, and increase field->PM handoff satisfaction from NPS 6 to >=8 in post-pilot survey. Constraints: must be usable by Solutions Engineers with 30 minutes of training, integrate with existing Linear ticketing (create parent/child relationships), and surface sensitive customer data only via secured links (no PII in brief). Deliverables: 1) SprintKit checklist + template (Confluence). 2) One-click Linear parent-ticket template with prefilled labels and link placeholders. 3) Scoring spreadsheet and example run for 3 pilot accounts. 4) Training micro-session + recording for CS. 5) Runbook for PM follow-up and handoff. Stakeholders: PM (Sofia Martinez), CS Enablement (Jamal Chen), Solutions Eng (Aisha Patel), Engineering lead (Maya Singh). Artifacts: Confluence draft: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/PM/field-to-feature-sprintkit, Example brief (Drive): https://drive.redwood.ai/drive/u/0/folders/1a2b3c, Pilot dashboard (Looker): https://looker.redwood.ai/dashboards/field-intake-pilot. Acceptance criteria: template used in 3 accounts with documented brief; PMs report brief contains enough detail to produce an initial estimate or schedule follow-up within 5 business days; duplicate ticket reductions observed in pilot cohort.
comments: 2026-01-29 — Kickoff: Workshop w/ CS (Jamal, Aisha) and PMs to map current signal paths. Noted three repeated friction points: inconsistent asks, missing success metrics, and unclear econ needs.

2026-02-03 — Draft sprint checklist uploaded to Confluence. Link shared to #cs-intake. Feedback: SEs want a canned 'example reply' for customers when requesting clarifying info. Action: add canned templates (SOF).

2026-02-10 — Rapid pilot with Account A and B scheduled. Created Linear parent ticket template (PM-709181-parent-template) and two child tickets to track briefs. Need automation to populate account labels and revenue tier.

2026-02-18 — Engineering review (Maya): recommends adding 'integration complexity' checkbox and pre-populated examples of similar features to speed triage. Trade-off: adding too many fields increases fill friction — decision: keep main template to 8 fields with optional advanced section.

2026-02-25 — CS Pilot run #1 complete. Observations: median time to brief = 48h, but econ proxy often missing. Action: include simple econ estimator table and a single-line ask for customer revenue impact. Assigned SE follow-up reminder (automation ticket ENG-20345).

2026-03-02 — PM review: brief quality good, two asks routed to backlog, one promoted to epic. Request from Sales leadership: add prioritization override for strategic accounts (manual flag + justifying note).
2026-03-08 — Legal review flagged potential PII in demo notes link. Mitigation: update runbook to require redaction and use secure Drive folder. Legal sign-off in progress.

2026-03-10 — Ready for pilot expansion checklist created. Next steps: train 10 SEs, enable automation to create Linear parent tickets, and run a 4-week pilot expansion for 15 accounts. Owner: Liam O'Connor.
